key_insight: TACIT repairs misspecified optimization models by combining LLM-guided structural reasoning with optimization-based validation and inference, so models can learn from past mistakes instead of overfitting sparse correction data.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a practical way to recover missing constraints, variables, and objectives in operational optimization models when expert knowledge is tacit and hard to formalize.
method: Top-down: an LLM proposes candidate repairs such as new constraints or variables.
Optimization then calibrates parameters and checks whether the proposed repair fits historical solution/override data.
Bottom-up: optimization extracts cuts from observed decisions, and the LLM turns them into interpretable modeling rules.
evidence_signal: Across 38 misspecification scenarios spanning nine optimization problem classes, TACIT repaired 78.9% of cases, outperforming the best baseline at 60.5%.
watch_item: Because repairs are learned from historical overrides, the approach may depend on data quality and still requires careful human review to avoid introducing plausible but incorrect constraints.
paper_title: TACIT: Optimization Models that Learn from Their Mistakes
